references.text: Direct parallel: the sources of the deep and the floodgates of heaven were closed, and the rain from heaven stopped - opposite to what happened in 7:11.

God separated the waters under the expanse from the waters above the expanse - this provides background for the 'sources of the deep' and the 'floodgates of heaven' that are opened in the flood narrative.
Mentions the sources of the deep (תהום) which God established, using the same expression as for the water sources that broke forth during the flood.
Uses similar imagery about the opening of the floodgates of heaven (אֲרֻבּוֹת), the same expression found in Genesis 7:11.
Mentions Noah's faith and godliness which led to the building of the ark, saving his household from the flood.
Refers directly to Noah's flood: the world at that time was destroyed when it was overwhelmed by water.
Refers to Noah's flood and how eight souls were saved through water.
The verses mark the two decisive moments of God's judgment and mercy in the Flood, emphasizing God's control over time and nature through parallel time references.
